messages:
maria: FYI we've started seeing slow memory growth on long-chat runs (100k+ tokens). Not a leak per-se, looks like KV cache fragmentation.
maria: repro on canary with `long-context-regression` profile.
raj: Can you paste the pmap / heap summary from the runner? also which allocator is in use (jemalloc/tcmalloc)?
kv-monitor-bot: metric snapshot: {"kv_cache_frag_ratio": "0.42", "kv_allocated_mb": "2480", "rss_mb": "2680", "long_context_tokens": "120000"}
oliver: ran an offline heap dump. pattern looks like many small "heaplets" tied to sequence prefixes. allocator rounds to 4096 so lots of internal waste when entries are ~600-2000 bytes.
oliver: profiling flamegraph shows heavy time in `kv_lookup` + GC churn around compaction windows.
sasha: thought: instead of slab-level compaction, what about a relinking compactor that coalesces live KV entries into compact pages and rebinds pointers atomically.
sasha: sketch:
```
// background compactor
for each shard:
  if frag_ratio > threshold && pause_budget_ok:
    reserve new_page
    for live_entry in shard.scan_live():
      copy entry -> new_page
      update pointer_map[entry.key] = new_page.offset
    atomic_swap(shard.page, new_page)
    free old pages lazily
```
sasha: benefits: avoids moving small holes around in-place, reduces per-entry copy overhead by bulk copying, allows switching to multiple smaller block sizes for new pages.
raj: Sounds promising. What's the expected pause? do we need stop-the-world for pointer map updates?
sasha: no STW if we use double-buffering + pointer indirection. reader path reads pointer_map[key] then follows to page. pointer updates are single word CAS.
maria: tradeoffs: extra indirection cost per lookup (one more memory read) vs reduced fragmentation. Need perf numbers on tail latency.
oliver: ran a microbench: lookup overhead ~1.6ns per token on x8664 with warm cache; end-to-end tail p95 for short requests unaffected, long-context throughput improved when frag_ratio>0.3.
raj: can we make this opt-in config so customers don't pay indirection cost unless needed?
sasha: yes. config:
```
kv.compaction.mode = "relinking" | "in-place"
kv.compaction.frag_threshold = 0.30
kv.compaction.scan_rate = "2MB/s"
kv.compaction.pause_budget_ms = 5
```
maria: also need safety: pointer_map corruption during failover. add versioned pointers and epoch-based reclamation.
oliver: cost model idea: estimate reclaimable_bytes/scan_cost and only trigger when reclaimable_bytes > k * scan_cost. we can tune k via A/B.
raj: perf regression note: one canary showed +8% CPU at p50 after enabling relinking because of extra loads; but p99 improved by 12% for long contexts.
sasha: let's run a 24h canary with mode=auto (enable relinking when frag>0.35) across two worker pools. collect metrics: cpu, p95/p99, kv_frag_ratio, rss, reclaimed_bytes.
maria: I'll own the canary. plan: roll to 10% traffic in staging tomorrow 09:00 UTC. raj, can you add the dashboard? oliver, add heap dump hook for quick diffs.
raj: adding dashboard panels and alert: kv_frag_ratio > 0.5 sustained -> rollback.
dev-bot: deploy scheduled for staging at 2026-03-18T09:00:00Z by maria (canary relinking experiment).
maria: one more question: block size options? current allocator rounding is 4KiB. we could add 1KiB page class for relinking pages to reduce internal slack for small entries.
oliver: tested 1KiB pages for new pages; fragmentation dropped 18% but lookup overhead slightly up. fine to keep as experimental.
sasha: I'll draft an RFC with design, correctness, and cost model. will include pseudo-code, benchmark scripts, and rollback plan.
maria: great. thanks all. please drop short notes in the RFC about backwards compatibility and KMS pointer encryption interaction.
raj: noted. will include telemetry and a/b plan.
oliver: 👍
sasha: :rocket:
